summary: Markets are broadly risk-on following a Democratic sweep of the U.S. Congress in the midterms, with Wall Street rallying on expectations that divided — or now Democrat-controlled — Washington will produce fewer sweeping policy disruptions, particularly around tariffs and deregulation. The midterm outcome is the dominant macro driver, reshaping expectations across energy policy, trade, and geopolitical posture, as the Democratic agenda pivots toward affordability and anti-corruption measures while Republican infighting intensifies over the Iran war and Trump's influence on the party. At the sector level, the post-election rally has exposed a sharp divide within the AI trade, with data center stocks sliding even as broader indices climbed, while mortgage lenders saw notable options activity and CVS was removed from CNBC's Bullpen watchlist, signaling deteriorating confidence in select healthcare names. Geopolitical risk remains elevated, with fresh U.S. sanctions targeting Indian and Turkish firms for aiding Iran adding friction to global trade relationships, and ongoing instability in Ukraine's security apparatus compounding uncertainty around Eastern European exposure. In the short term, the market's constructive tone could persist if political gridlock is confirmed and macro data cooperates, but investors will closely monitor sanctions escalation, energy policy shifts under Democratic leadership, and any further fracturing of the AI sector narrative.
